did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with the declaration, “The LORD reigns,” and describes a worldwide response to the LORD’s kingship: the earth rejoices, and the many islands are glad.
Did you know? Clouds and thick darkness surround the LORD’s appearing, but at the heart of the description are “righteousness and justice”—the foundations of his throne and kingdom.
Did you know? The fire in this psalm is described as going before the LORD and consuming his enemies all around him, emphasizing the power of his appearance and his judgment on the wicked.
Did you know? His lightning lights up the whole world, and the earth is portrayed as seeing it and trembling; all of nature responds to the divine revelation.
Did you know? The melting of the mountains “like wax” is a vivid picture of utter weakness before the LORD, who is called here “the Lord of all the earth.”
Did you know? The heavens themselves are described as proclaiming the LORD’s righteousness, while all the nations see his glory—a picture of worldwide recognition of his kingship.
Did you know? The psalm contrasts those who worship idols and boast in false gods with the recognition of the LORD’s supremacy: all powers are called to bow down before him.
Did you know? Zion and the towns of Judah rejoice when they hear the LORD’s judgments—in other words, their joy is connected with divine justice being revealed and carried out in the world.

Did you know? In this psalm, loving the LORD is also presented as a moral commitment: those who love him are called to hate evil, and the LORD is described as guarding the lives of his faithful ones and rescuing them from the wicked.
Did you know? The phrase “Light is sown for the righteous” presents light as something planted that will eventually grow and be revealed, alongside the joy promised to the upright in heart.
